rule.sl:
Pridevnik pove, kakšna je stvar, prislov pa, kako kdo nekaj dela: **a slow walk** (počasen sprehod), a **Jack walks slowly.** (Jack hodi počasi.)

Večina dobi **-ly**: **quietly**, **quickly**. **-ful** obdrži oba l (**carefully**); soglasnik + **-y** postane **-ily** (**happily**, **easily**); končni **-le** postane **-ly** (**gently**, **terribly**).

Posebne: **good, well** (**She sings well.**, nikoli *sings good*). **fast**, **hard**, **late**, **early** se ne spremenijo: **He runs fast.**, nikoli *fastly*. **hardly** (komaj) in **lately** (zadnje čase) sta drugi besedi.

Kam: za glagol, in za predmet, če ga glagol ima: **Sam plays darts well.**, nikoli *Sam plays well darts.* Prislov na **-ly** lahko stoji tudi pred glagolom: **Jack quietly closed the gate.**

Za **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell**, **taste** pride pridevnik: **The soup smells good.** **You look tired.** **friendly** in **lovely** sta pridevnika, čeprav se končata na **-ly**.

Primerjava: **faster**, **harder**, **better**, **worse**, **more slowly**, **more carefully**.
rule.de:
Ein Adjektiv sagt, wie etwas ist, ein Adverb, wie man etwas tut: **a slow walk** (eine langsame Wanderung), aber **Jack walks slowly.** (Jack geht langsam.) Das Deutsche sagt beides gleich.

Die meisten bekommen **-ly**: **quietly**, **quickly**. **-ful** behält beide l (**carefully**); Konsonant + **-y** wird zu **-ily** (**happily**, **easily**); **-le** am Ende wird zu **-ly** (**gently**, **terribly**).

Eigen: **good, well** (**She sings well.**, nie *sings good*). **fast**, **hard**, **late**, **early** bleiben gleich: **He runs fast.**, nie *fastly*. **hardly** (kaum) und **lately** (in letzter Zeit) sind andere Wörter.

Wohin: nach dem Verb, und nach dem Objekt, wenn es eins hat: **Sam plays darts well.**, nie *Sam plays well darts.* Ein Adverb auf **-ly** kann auch vor dem Verb stehen: **Jack quietly closed the gate.**

Nach **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell**, **taste** kommt ein Adjektiv: **The soup smells good.** **You look tired.** **friendly** und **lovely** sind Adjektive, trotz **-ly**.

Vergleich: **faster**, **harder**, **better**, **worse**, **more slowly**, **more carefully**.
rule.it:
L'aggettivo dice com'è una cosa, l'avverbio come si fa qualcosa: **a slow walk** (una camminata lenta), ma **Jack walks slowly.** (Jack cammina lentamente.)

La maggior parte prende **-ly**: **quietly**, **quickly**. **-ful** tiene le due l (**carefully**); consonante + **-y** diventa **-ily** (**happily**, **easily**); **-le** finale diventa **-ly** (**gently**, **terribly**).

A parte: **good, well** (**She sings well.**, mai *sings good*). **fast**, **hard**, **late**, **early** non cambiano: **He runs fast.**, mai *fastly*. **hardly** (appena) e **lately** (ultimamente) sono altre parole.

Dove: dopo il verbo, e dopo il complemento se c'è: **Sam plays darts well.**, mai *Sam plays well darts.* Un avverbio in **-ly** può stare anche prima del verbo: **Jack quietly closed the gate.**

Dopo **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell**, **taste** viene un aggettivo: **The soup smells good.** **You look tired.** **friendly** e **lovely** sono aggettivi, anche se finiscono in **-ly**.

Per confrontare: **faster**, **harder**, **better**, **worse**, **more slowly**, **more carefully**.
rule.en:
An adjective says what a thing is like, an adverb how something is done: **a slow walk**, but **Jack walks slowly.**

Most take **-ly**: **quietly**, **quickly**. **-ful** keeps both l's (**carefully**); a consonant + **-y** becomes **-ily** (**happily**, **easily**); a final **-le** becomes **-ly** (**gently**, **terribly**).

On their own: **good, well**: **She sings well.** (never *She sings good.*) **fast**, **hard**, **late**, **early** don't change: **He runs fast.** (never *He runs fastly.*) **hardly** (almost not) and **lately** (recently) are other words.

Where: after the verb, and after its object if it has one: **Sam plays darts well.** (never *Sam plays well darts.*) A **-ly** adverb can also stand before the verb: **Jack quietly closed the gate.**

After **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell**, **taste** comes an adjective: **The soup smells good.** **You look tired.** **friendly** and **lovely** are adjectives, though they end in **-ly**.

To compare: **faster**, **harder**, **better**, **worse**, **more slowly**, **more carefully**.
